problems: The blind guess (a human figure with outstretched arms and spread legs) does not match the intended subject. The title and the part labels (beak tip, crown, wings, forked tail) describe a bird, and the drawing reads as a bird, not a person. There are no legs; the lower stars form a forked tail.
The figure is the right way up: head and beak at top (beak tip 94490 at about (340,110)), tail at bottom (base 96825 at about (222,458)).

The head is a small loop at the top, the beak is a single gold line, and the neck and breast run diagonally down to the body. Crown 94302 sits just under the beak tip rather than on a distinct head shape.

The body stars are not placed well. Belly 95853 (about (289,278)) and lower body 96441 (about (262,318)) sit almost on top of each other and on the left-wrist star 98571, so the labels overlap and are hard to read.

The left wing is a single gold line from the wrist to the wingtip (99675 at about (89,406)), with a separate leading-edge star 99848. The leading edge and wingtip are close together and read as one line.
The right wing is a triangle from breast/belly out to wingtip 92689 (about (447,289)) and primary 93408 (about (425,397)). It is the clearest wing shape in the figure.
The tail fork is cramped. Base 96825 (about (222,458)), left fork tip 97165 and right fork tip 96459 (about (262,470)) are within a few pixels, so the fork does not show as two tines.

The blue outline is a loose, wiggly trace that wanders outside the gold skeleton, so it does not read as a clean silhouette. The gold lines dominate, so the figure reads more as a stick skeleton than a filled bird shape.
Several text labels overlap the drawing and each other (belly, lower body, left wrist, left tail fork tip, base of forked tail), which makes the atlas hard to read.
output.advice: Redraw as a clear bird silhouette, upright, with the head at top and the tail at bottom. Keep the current overall layout but fix these points: (1) Head: draw a rounded head shape around crown 94302 (about (348,130)), with beak tip 94490 (about (340,110)) as a short pointed beak on the upper left, so the head reads as a head. (2) Neck and breast: put breast 94779 (about (338,230)) where the neck meets the body, with a smooth curve from the head down to it. (3) Body: move belly 95853 to the centre of a teardrop body, about (290,280), and move lower body 96441 down to about (275,320) under the wing roots so the two stars do not stack. (4) Wings: left wing from the body out to the wrist 98571 (about (152,318)), then down to the leading-edge star 99848 and wingtip 99675 (about (89,406)); right wing as a fuller curved shape from the body out to wingtip 92689 (about (447,289)), with primary 93408 (about (425,397)) on its trailing edge. (5) Tail: spread the fork. Base 96825 at about (222,458), with left fork tip 97165 and right fork tip 96459 pulled further apart (for example one about 30px left and one about 40px right of the base, both lower) so two distinct tines show. (6) Outline: replace the wandering blue trace with a closed filled silhouette following the same stars, and make the gold lines follow its edges. (7) Labels: shorten them or move them to leader lines in open space, so none overlap the figure or each other."]
